open_points.subject: A17 listener exclusivity
open_points.text: Registry binds each listener exclusively — it sets no option that lets a second active socket bind an overlapping endpoint
open_points.question: What exactly counts as an overlapping endpoint: only the identical host and port, or also wildcard/specific-address pairs and other address ranges that accept some of the same connections?
options: Only an identical host and port must be excluded
Any listeners with the same port and intersecting accepted-address sets must be excluded
Use the platform's native definition of a conflicting bind
open_points.default_guess: Treat any same-port listeners whose accepted-address sets intersect as overlapping.

events: Another process attempts to bind `127.0.0.1:8781` while Registry is running.
outcomes: The bind fails because the wildcard and loopback listeners overlap.
The bind may succeed because only an identical configured endpoint is prohibited.
witness.observer: The process attempting the second bind and clients connecting through loopback

open_points.subject: A21 security review basis for A17 listener addresses
open_points.text: R0-19 keeps which network may reach each surface the deployment's
open_points.question: May A21 and A17 still rely on R0-19, or must they name the replacement decisions that now govern reachability?
options: R0-19 remains the governing basis for deployment reachability
R0-19 is replaced, as its own passage says, so the review must rely on R0-27, R0-28, R0-29, R0-39 and R0-48 as applicable
A17 itself now owns the complete reachability rule
open_points.default_guess: Treat R0-19 as replaced and rewrite the review basis to cite the applicable replacement decisions.
